title: Screen console & virtual terminals
summary: Each target boots behind the Breenix logo and hands the screen to a text console sized for its display, with six virtual terminals that keep their own screens, scrollback and sessions, switched by ioctl, chvt and the keyboard, each screen checked by reading its displayed pixels back.

cases.title: Text written to tty1 is drawn on the screen
The displayed pixels read back identical to the console's shadow
The read-back is of the resource bound to the scanout, after a completed flush
Drawn cells match the glyphs the font oracle expects
The font size and grid follow the size rule for the display
The cursor band is drawn in the cursor cell and in no other cell
Kernel records at INFO and above appear on tty1 while no login session holds it
Only warnings and errors are drawn once a login session holds tty1
The console does not draw while a process owns the display
Giving the display back redraws the foreground terminal
SGR selects the 16 colours and their bright forms
256-colour and 24-bit colours map to the nearest of the 16 by the contract's rule
Bold draws the bold weight, reverse swaps the pair and underline draws its row
UTF-8 Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A characters draw their glyphs
Malformed UTF-8 and characters outside the repertoire draw one cell of ?
Box-drawing characters draw the generated glyphs at the cell size
DECSTBM limits scrolling to the region
IL and DL insert and delete lines within the scroll region
ICH, DCH and ECH insert, delete and erase characters
DECSC and DECRC save and restore the cursor and attributes
CSI ?25l hides the cursor and CSI ?25h shows it
With autowrap off, characters past the last column overwrite it
Tab stops start at each 8th column and HTS and TBC set and clear them
CSI ?1049 switches to a cleared alternate screen and back to the saved one
ESC c resets the screen, cursor, attributes, tab stops and modes
CSI 6n answers the cursor position on the terminal's input
tty1 to tty6 exist with their device numbers and open independently
/dev/console and /dev/tty1 are the same terminal
/dev/tty0 reaches the foreground terminal
/dev/tty opens the caller's controlling terminal when it is a VT
/dev/tty fails with ENXIO without a controlling terminal
Each terminal keeps its own termios
Each terminal is the controlling terminal of its own session
TIOCGWINSZ reports the size rule's grid on each terminal
/dev/vcsN reads the screen text, with ? for characters past Latin-1
/dev/vcsaN reads the header and the displayed colour pair of each cell
Output to a terminal in the background is on its screen when it returns
A process on a terminal in the background keeps running
A read on a terminal in the background waits and takes keyboard input once it is in the foreground
A switch sends no signal and leaves each foreground process group unchanged
VT_ACTIVATE switches the foreground terminal
VT_ACTIVATE outside 1 to 6 fails with ENXIO
VT_WAITACTIVE returns once the terminal is in the foreground
VT_WAITACTIVE returns only after the new screen is on the display
A signal interrupts VT_WAITACTIVE with EINTR
VT_GETSTATE reports the foreground terminal and the open ones
VT_OPENQRY reports the lowest terminal no process has open
In KD_GRAPHICS the kernel does not draw the terminal, and KD_TEXT redraws it
When a KD_GRAPHICS owner exits, its terminal returns to KD_TEXT and is redrawn
Switching away from a display owner without VT_PROCESS fails with EBUSY
A VT_PROCESS owner gets its release signal and the switch waits for VT_RELDISP
A VT_PROCESS owner gets its acquire signal and answers with VT_ACKACQ
VT_RELDISP 0 refuses the release and the terminal stays in the foreground
An owner that does not answer within 3 s keeps the terminal
An owner that exits while a release is pending lets the switch proceed
During a pending release the latest request names the target
A request for the releasing terminal cancels the switch and signals acquire
VT_SETMODE on a terminal another live process owns fails with EBUSY
VT_RELDISP with no answer pending, or from another process, fails
A process neither root nor on a terminal gets EPERM for the changing requests
After a switch the displayed pixels read back identical to the new terminal's screen
A switch logs the terminal number and a digest, not the screen's text
Lines scrolled off the screen are kept in the terminal's scrollback
Each terminal has its own scrollback
A terminal's scrollback and view survive switches
New output does not move a scrolled-back view
A key that sends input returns the view to the live screen
chvt N switches to terminal N and exits 0
chvt returns only once the terminal is in the foreground
chvt with a number outside 1 to 6 exits 1 with the error
Each of tty1 to tty6 shows the login prompt, read back from its own screen
A wrong password is refused on a numbered terminal
The per-run account logs in on a numbered terminal
After logout the terminal's getty is respawned and prompts again
Sessions on two terminals have their own controlling terminals and process groups
Alt+F1 to F6 switch from a text terminal
Ctrl+Alt+F1 to F6 switch from a text terminal
Ctrl+Alt+Fn switches away from a graphics terminal whose owner chose VT_PROCESS
On a graphics terminal Alt+Fn is input to the terminal and does not switch
Alt+Left and Alt+Right select the previous and next terminal, wrapping within 1 to 6
Alt+F7 to F12 on a text terminal do not switch and send no bytes
Keyboard input reaches only the foreground terminal
Ctrl+C signals only the foreground terminal's foreground process group
Caps Lock state is kept per terminal
Shift+PageUp and Shift+PageDown move the view by half a screen
A cursor report joins the partly typed canonical line, after its keys
